{"notes":"HSA/FSA flag (is_hsa_fsa) — decision + open question (2026-07-01, tuily):

KEEP the payments.is_hsa_fsa column. FT9 (docs: product/features/FT-signup-payment-flow.md) makes 'HSA/FSA card flagged correctly on receipt' a GO-LIVE acceptance criterion, so the per-payment flag is required.

BUT the detection mechanism FT9 assumes is NOT possible. Confirmed against current Stripe docs:
- Stripe has NO API-level HSA/FSA detection. Support page: 'Stripe does not provide API-level detection for HSA/FSA cards.'
- PaymentMethod.card exposes no health-benefit field and NO full BIN/IIN — only last4. funding is credit|debit|prepaid|unknown (prepaid is a weak, unreliable proxy).
- So FT9's 'HSA/FSA card detected on the Stripe Customer object' cannot be implemented — Stripe surfaces no such data. This resolves the open standup item (2026-06-08: validate Stripe HSA/FSA config steps).
- Stripe's own receipt shows nothing about HSA/FSA and only itemizes invoice/subscription payments (ours is a one-off PaymentIntent) — hence the custom Resend receipt (FT11/D11) is required.
- Acceptance itself is purely account config: HSA/FSA-eligible MCC (8011/8099). SIGIS/IIAS only applies to merchants selling products, not a medical service — so we're on the simpler MCC path.

PROPOSED populator: user self-select checkbox ('I'm paying with an HSA/FSA card') → is_hsa_fsa. SAQ-A-safe (no PAN), self-reported (not financial truth). funding==prepaid could prefill only.

OPEN — needs PM sign-off: is a self-select checkbox acceptable to satisfy the FT9 receipt-flag requirement, given Stripe can't auto-detect? Checkbox NOT built yet (deferred out of the test-mode demo)."}

{"description":"After the user submits their email in the marketing booking flow, resume them at the correct point. NEW users go straight into the modal at the first step; RETURNING (known) users see a "Welcome back" screen and must confirm via an emailed link before resuming at their first incomplete step. If everything is already complete, hand off to the funnel.

Figma:
- Welcome-back screen ("Already in database"): https://www.figma.com/design/SppKdzsaH6rQ14u90UpNSq/Primary-Brain-Health?node-id=896-1479&m=dev

## Flow
1. Booking form email submit -> resolveBookingProgress(email) looks up the user.
2. NEW email -> create user (createAccountCore) -> open modal at "details" (no confirmation needed; nothing to protect).
3. RETURNING email (user exists, not fully complete) -> show the "Welcome back, {firstName}" modal (Figma 896-1479) and SEND a confirmation email. Do NOT open the step modal yet.
4. User clicks the emailed magic link -> verify token -> resume the booking modal at the FIRST INCOMPLETE step (details -> consent -> payment) computed by resolveBookingProgress.
5. Already fully complete (details + consent + succeeded payment) -> hand off to funnel /login?email= (same as DoneStep) -> /assessments.

## Welcome back screen (Figma 896-1479, "Extra Information" card)
- Title: "Welcome back, {firstName}"
- Body: "You already started the process previously. We’ve sent you an email. Please check your inbox, and confirm this is you."
- CTA: "Continue Where I left" (re-send/return affordance; the actual resume happens via the emailed link).
- Rendered as a modal/card over the booking section; reuse the existing Modal shell (apps/marketing/src/components/booking/Modal.tsx) + @pbh/ui + tokens.

## Current behavior (to change)
- BookingStepFlow.tsx uses a useState stepIndex over MODAL_STEPS = ["details","consent","payment","done"]; start() HARDCODES setStepIndex(0). advance() uses Math.min, so starting mid-sequence already works.
- Email is collected by inline SignupForm (first/last/email) -> signupAction (apps/marketing/src/components/booking/actions.ts) -> createAccountCore (packages/booking/src/server/signup-core.ts), which INSERTs a users row and REJECTS duplicate emails ("account already exists"). Must change to lookup-or-create.

## Completeness signals (all NEW reads; consents/payments are write-only today)
- details incomplete if users.dateOfBirth is null (also stateOfResidence, phone, gender, educationLevel, patientIdentification; message optional). packages/db/src/schema/users.ts; set by details-core.ts.
- consent incomplete if no consents row for user_id. packages/db/src/schema/consents.ts.
- payment incomplete if no payments row with status="succeeded" for user_id. packages/db/src/schema/payments.ts (fulfill.ts recordSucceededPayment). A bare row is NOT sufficient (failed/refunded can exist).

## Implementation
1. resolveBookingProgress core in packages/booking/src/server/ (e.g. booking-progress.ts): normalize email; SELECT users WHERE email = ? (pattern in register-and-enroll.ts:499-519). No user -> createAccountCore -> step "details" (new-user path). User exists -> first incomplete step, or "complete". Returns { userId, email, firstName, step:"details"|"consent"|"payment"|"complete", isReturning:boolean }.
2. Returning + not complete -> render Welcome back modal + trigger sendResumeConfirmationEmail(userId). Wire signupAction accordingly.
3. Extend SignupState/SignupResult (packages/booking/src/types.ts) to carry step + isReturning (+ complete).
4. BookingStepFlow.start(): for the new-user path, setStepIndex(Math.max(0, MODAL_STEPS.indexOf(step))); for returning, show Welcome back modal instead; if step==="complete", navigate to ${NEXT_PUBLIC_FUNNEL_URL}/login?email=... (reuse DoneStep handoff).
5. Magic-link resume: verify route validates the token and opens the booking modal at the resolved first-incomplete step.

## Email confirmation infrastructure (NEW PREREQUISITE - none exists today)
There is NO email-sending setup in the repo (no resend/nodemailer/sendgrid/ses, no token/verify code). This feature needs:
- An email-sending capability + provider (recommend Resend; works cleanly on Vercel) + a confirmation email template.
- A confirmation token: signed (HMAC/JWT, short TTL) OR a DB table (e.g. booking_resume_tokens with expiry) tied to userId + intended step; single-use.
- A verify/resume route that validates the token and enters the resumed flow.
This is sizable and separable; consider splitting it into its own prerequisite sub-task that this one depends on.

## Security / privacy
The email confirmation is the mitigation for unauthenticated resume + PII/enumeration: DO NOT open the step modal or reveal stored data on bare email entry. To avoid account enumeration, show the same "we’ve sent you an email" outcome whether or not the email exists (only send the email when it does). Tokens must be single-use + short-lived. Revisit with real auth (resolveBookingUserId is a TODO(clerk)).

## Acceptance criteria
- New email -> modal opens at details (no email confirmation).
- Returning email (partial) -> Welcome back modal shown + confirmation email sent; step modal NOT opened until the emailed link is clicked; link resumes at the correct first incomplete step (consent if details done; payment if details+consent done).
- Fully-onboarded/paid email -> handed off to funnel /login -> /assessments.
- Bare email entry never reveals whether an account exists nor exposes stored PII; tokens single-use + expiring.
- Payment completeness uses status="succeeded", not just a row.

## Verification
Seed users at each state (new/partial/complete) in a test DB. pnpm --filter marketing dev (:3000); submit each email and confirm: new -> details; returning -> Welcome back + email; click link -> resumes at expected step; complete -> funnel handoff. pnpm typecheck + lint."}

{"id":"pbh-bq8","title":"Resume booking modal at the first incomplete step after email submit","description":"After the user submits their email in the marketing booking flow, resume them at the correct point. NEW users go straight into the modal at the first step; RETURNING (known) users see a "Welcome back" screen and must confirm via an emailed link before resuming at their first incomplete step. If everything is already complete, hand off to the funnel.

Figma:
- Welcome-back screen ("Already in database"): https://www.figma.com/design/SppKdzsaH6rQ14u90UpNSq/Primary-Brain-Health?node-id=896-1479&m=dev

## Flow
1. Booking form email submit -> resolveBookingProgress(email) looks up the user.
2. NEW email -> create user (createAccountCore) -> open modal at "details" (no confirmation needed; nothing to protect).
3. RETURNING email (user exists, not fully complete) -> show the "Welcome back, {firstName}" modal (Figma 896-1479) and SEND a confirmation email. Do NOT open the step modal yet.
4. User clicks the emailed magic link -> verify token -> resume the booking modal at the FIRST INCOMPLETE step (details -> consent -> payment) computed by resolveBookingProgress.
5. Already fully complete (details + consent + succeeded payment) -> hand off to funnel /login?email= (same as DoneStep) -> /assessments.

## Welcome back screen (Figma 896-1479, "Extra Information" card)
- Title: "Welcome back, {firstName}"
- Body: "You already started the process previously. We’ve sent you an email. Please check your inbox, and confirm this is you."
- CTA: "Continue Where I left" (re-send/return affordance; the actual resume happens via the emailed link).
- Rendered as a modal/card over the booking section; reuse the existing Modal shell (apps/marketing/src/components/booking/Modal.tsx) + @pbh/ui + tokens.

## Current behavior (to change)
- BookingStepFlow.tsx uses a useState stepIndex over MODAL_STEPS = ["details","consent","payment","done"]; start() HARDCODES setStepIndex(0). advance() uses Math.min, so starting mid-sequence already works.
- Email is collected by inline SignupForm (first/last/email) -> signupAction (apps/marketing/src/components/booking/actions.ts) -> createAccountCore (packages/booking/src/server/signup-core.ts), which INSERTs a users row and REJECTS duplicate emails ("account already exists"). Must change to lookup-or-create.

## Completeness signals (all NEW reads; consents/payments are write-only today)
- details incomplete if users.dateOfBirth is null (also stateOfResidence, phone, gender, educationLevel, patientIdentification; message optional). packages/db/src/schema/users.ts; set by details-core.ts.
- consent incomplete if no consents row for user_id. packages/db/src/schema/consents.ts.
- payment incomplete if no payments row with status="succeeded" for user_id. packages/db/src/schema/payments.ts (fulfill.ts recordSucceededPayment). A bare row is NOT sufficient (failed/refunded can exist).

## Implementation
1. resolveBookingProgress core in packages/booking/src/server/ (e.g. booking-progress.ts): normalize email; SELECT users WHERE email = ? (pattern in register-and-enroll.ts:499-519). No user -> createAccountCore -> step "details" (new-user path). User exists -> first incomplete step, or "complete". Returns { userId, email, firstName, step:"details"|"consent"|"payment"|"complete", isReturning:boolean }.
2. Returning + not complete -> render Welcome back modal + trigger sendResumeConfirmationEmail(userId). Wire signupAction accordingly.
3. Extend SignupState/SignupResult (packages/booking/src/types.ts) to carry step + isReturning (+ complete).
4. BookingStepFlow.start(): for the new-user path, setStepIndex(Math.max(0, MODAL_STEPS.indexOf(step))); for returning, show Welcome back modal instead; if step==="complete", navigate to ${NEXT_PUBLIC_FUNNEL_URL}/login?email=... (reuse DoneStep handoff).
5. Magic-link resume: verify route validates the token and opens the booking modal at the resolved first-incomplete step.

## Email confirmation infrastructure (NEW PREREQUISITE - none exists today)
There is NO email-sending setup in the repo (no resend/nodemailer/sendgrid/ses, no token/verify code). This feature needs:
- An email-sending capability + provider (recommend Resend; works cleanly on Vercel) + a confirmation email template.
- A confirmation token: signed (HMAC/JWT, short TTL) OR a DB table (e.g. booking_resume_tokens with expiry) tied to userId + intended step; single-use.
- A verify/resume route that validates the token and enters the resumed flow.
This is sizable and separable; consider splitting it into its own prerequisite sub-task that this one depends on.

## Security / privacy
The email confirmation is the mitigation for unauthenticated resume + PII/enumeration: DO NOT open the step modal or reveal stored data on bare email entry. To avoid account enumeration, show the same "we’ve sent you an email" outcome whether or not the email exists (only send the email when it does). Tokens must be single-use + short-lived. Revisit with real auth (resolveBookingUserId is a TODO(clerk)).

## Acceptance criteria
- New email -> modal opens at details (no email confirmation).
- Returning email (partial) -> Welcome back modal shown + confirmation email sent; step modal NOT opened until the emailed link is clicked; link resumes at the correct first incomplete step (consent if details done; payment if details+consent done).
- Fully-onboarded/paid email -> handed off to funnel /login -> /assessments.
- Bare email entry never reveals whether an account exists nor exposes stored PII; tokens single-use + expiring.
- Payment completeness uses status="succeeded", not just a row.

## Verification
Seed users at each state (new/partial/complete) in a test DB. pnpm --filter marketing dev (:3000); submit each email and confirm: new -> details; returning -> Welcome back + email; click link -> resumes at expected step; complete -> funnel handoff. pnpm typecheck + lint.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"feature","owner":"brizolla.tuily@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-07-20T18:07:19Z","created_by":"tuily","updated_at":"2026-07-20T18:22:25Z"}

Background (Stefanie, Slack): HIPAA does not prescribe a specific session-timeout duration — it requires an automatic logoff control based on the organization's risk assessment. Because the authenticated dashboard provides access to the Linus report, the dashboard session becomes part of the protected access pathway even though the report itself stays stored in Linus.

Controls to document:
- 15-minute inactivity timeout on the authenticated dashboard
- 8-hour absolute session cap, so an active session cannot remain authenticated indefinitely
- single-use sign-in link with a 10–15 minute TTL (applies if magic links are chosen)
- scope: the ENTIRE authenticated dashboard, not only the report page

Note: the doc's current "Session strategy" section specifies a 30-day sliding expiration. That must be replaced, not appended to.

Deliberately NOT included: a step-up re-authentication gate before opening or downloading the report. Stefanie raised it in the original thread, but it was dropped from scope — the idle + absolute timeouts are the control set we are committing to. Revisit only if compliance asks for it again.
"}

{"description":"Update the booking flow to the reworked Figma designs. Scope grew beyond a restyle — Arian re-cut the steps, so this covers signup, details, the schema, and a Linus defect the new design exposed.

Figma: signup 1181:1719 · details/self 1181:1970 · details/someone-else 1181:2191

## What changed
- **"Who is this consultation for?" moved from the bottom of details to the top of signup.** It decides what every other field means, so asking it last left users entering a DOB and ZIP without knowing whose. Captured by `createAccountCore` into the existing `users.patient_identification`.
- **Details swaps subcopy, not labels.** "…about yourself" vs "…about the person receiving care", instead of prefixing every label with "Patient ".
- **Patient first/last name row** renders in details only for someone-else bookings. New nullable columns `users.patient_first_name` / `patient_last_name` (migration 0009).
- **Linus subject fix** — `buildRegisterInput` sent the buyer's name with the patient's DOB/gender, producing a subject that was half one person and half the other. It now registers the patient when the booking is for someone else, keeping the account holder's email. Throws `MissingPatientNameError` rather than falling back to the buyer.
- `SegmentedControl` 52px → 48px to match the field height; `labelClass` exported from `@pbh/ui` for the radio group's visible caption.

## Deliberate divergences from the frames
- **State of residence is kept**, though absent from every frame — the RFP requires it for the primary-care handoff and the intake gate's eligibility check (PBH_Website_v2.1_RFP.md:95, SOW2-Proposal-v5-no-pricing.md:175). Linus does not consume it. It is paired with education to preserve the two-up rhythm.
- **Full date of birth**, not the year-only Select in the older 751:* frames — the newer frames agree ("Birthday MM/DD/YYYY") and it matches `users.date_of_birth`.
- **No free-text concerns field.** The new frames dropped it, matching the compliance removal in PR #21 (pbh-4il / pbh-h9i).

- Every frame is drawn as a modal card with an X close, **including signup** — but signup is currently inline on the marketing page. Kept inline; moving it into the modal is a larger flow change.

- `buildRegisterInput` asserted directly for both branches plus the missing-name guard.

Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/SppKdzsaH6rQ14u90UpNSq/Primary-Brain-Health?node-id=1088-4452&m=dev

## The design (node 1088:4452)

Section header "Start with a brain health consultation" + subcopy, then **two side-by-side package cards** (610px each), then a full-width HSA/FSA note: "Both services may be eligible for HSA/FSA reimbursement, depending on your plan. We can provide documentation to support submission."

**Basic Assessment Package — $149** — CTA "Book Basic Assessment"
- Brain health assessment (taken online)
- A personal consultation with a brain health specialist
- Clear explanation of findings and risk profile
- Personalized lifestyle recommendations and next steps

**Comprehensive Assessment Package — $449** — CTA "Book Comprehensive Assessment"
- Everything in the Basic Assessment.
- Physician Assessment.
- A diagnosis from a clinician
- Ongoing treatment options with medication and doctor referrals
- Continuous support from a brain health specialist

**There is no inline signup form in this design.** Each card's CTA opens the booking modal, which now starts at signup.

## What this touches

- `apps/marketing/src/components/booking/BookingSection.tsx` — currently a two-column layout: copy + inline `SignupForm` on the left, a single `IncludesPanel` on the right. Becomes header + two cards + the HSA/FSA note.
- `apps/marketing/src/components/booking/IncludesPanel.tsx` — currently hardcodes one price and six bullets. Becomes a reusable card taking name/price/bullets/CTA. Its inline check SVG should use `CheckIcon` from `@pbh/ui` (added in PR #20) or `PhosphorIcon name="SealCheck"` — the design uses SealCheck.
- `apps/marketing/src/components/booking/BookingStepFlow.tsx` — `MODAL_STEPS` is currently `["details","consent","payment","done"]` with signup inline on the page. Add `signup` as the first modal step and open the modal from each card's CTA. This resolves the open question flagged on PR #22: every Figma frame draws signup as a modal card, but it was left inline because moving it was out of that PR's scope.

## Known blockers — these are the real work, not the layout

1. **Pricing is single-product.** `packages/payments/src/pricing.ts` resolves ONE price from `STRIPE_ASSESSMENT_PRICE_ID` (`env.ts:27`) and memoises it in a module-level `cached` singleton. Two packages need two Stripe prices, a per-package lookup, and a cache keyed by package rather than one slot. `checkout-core.ts` builds the Session from that single entry.
2. **The chosen package isn't captured anywhere.** `payments` records only `amount_cents` — no price/product reference. The selection has to be carried from the card CTA through signup → details → consent → payment, and stored, or we can't tell afterwards which package someone bought.
3. **Comprehensive is not just a bigger Linus enrollment.** "Physician Assessment", "A diagnosis from a clinician", and "Ongoing treatment options with medication and doctor referrals" are clinical services beyond the Linus assessment. Decide what the funnel actually provisions for $449 — a different Linus campaign (`packages/linus/src/campaigns.ts`), a manual clinical workflow, or something else. **Confirm with David/Stefanie before building.** This also has compliance weight: "a diagnosis from a clinician" moves the product further from the wellness framing the consent copy currently uses.

## Open questions
- Does the $449 package change the consent text? The current wellness + HIPAA NPP consent (`pbh-3v0`) is written for a wellness assessment, not a diagnostic service.
- Should the two cards be Tina-editable, or hardcoded? `BookingSection` currently takes `headline`/`subheadline` as props bound to a Tina block.

## Acceptance criteria
- Section matches the frame: header, two package cards with the exact copy above, HSA/FSA note.
- Each CTA opens the booking modal starting at signup; the chosen package is carried through the flow and recorded.
- Checkout charges the correct Stripe price per package (from the catalog, not a hardcoded amount — see pbh-ggr / PR #16).
- Matches Figma in-browser (computed styles, not class names); no raw hex.
- `pnpm typecheck` + lint changed files.

Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/SppKdzsaH6rQ14u90UpNSq/Primary-Brain-Health

DESIGN -> STEP MAPPING (all 5 already exist as funnel DEMO code, being re-homed to marketing):
- 360-2502  Landing booking section 'Start With a Brain Health assessment & Consultation' (First/Last/Email + Includes checklist + $149 / HSA-FSA note). Ref: apps/funnel .../signup/SignupForm.tsx + marketing IntakeForm block.
- 360-2854  Modal 1 'Welcome, {name}' details (DOB, gender, ZIP, phone, education, concerns). Ref: apps/funnel .../details/DetailsForm.tsx.
- 466-245 / 360-3214  Modal 2 'Almost there!' terms; scroll-to-enable -> 'Continue With Payment'. Ref: apps/funnel .../consent/ConsentForm.tsx.
- 360-3226  Modal 3 'Payment' — Stripe Embedded Checkout. Ref: apps/funnel .../payment/PaymentStep.tsx.

DECISIONS (from user):
- Flow lives ENTIRELY on the marketing site, presented as a MODAL sequence.
- Funnel /get-started stepper was DEMO scaffolding — not the production surface (retire it).
- Scope = full end-to-end.

BACKEND RECOMMENDATION — consolidate server logic into marketing via shared workspace packages (not copy-paste, not cross-app API):
- @pbh/db       Drizzle schema + migrations + Neon client (from apps/funnel/src/db)
- @pbh/payments Stripe server helpers + Checkout Session + webhook (from apps/funnel/src/lib/stripe)
- @pbh/linus    enrollment client (from apps/funnel/src/lib/linus)
- Re-home the 4 step server actions (createAccount, completeProfile, recordConsent, createAssessmentCheckoutSession/finalizeCheckoutSession) as MARKETING server actions calling those packages.
Rejected: marketing-calls-funnel-API (cross-origin CORS/cookie/iframe-Stripe friction); copy-paste rebuild (duplication/drift).

SHARED UI -> promote to @pbh/ui (shared UI only, never business logic): StepHeader, FieldError, Label, field/textarea class constants, 'Myself / Someone Else' segmented control, styled <select>.

OPEN ITEMS (non-blocking):
- Does the funnel keep /assessments + /login? If yes -> they consume @pbh/db/@pbh/linus; if funnel fully retired -> fold packages into marketing.
- Design tokens: Figma uses teal (#006e8a primary/CTA, #f5f3ee input bg, #224b60 Includes card) vs codebase Cognitive Sanctuary (navy #041632, forest #446558). Confirm whether teal is new brand primary or maps to existing tokens (see [deleted:pbh-bws.39]).

SUB-WORK CHECKLIST:
[ ] Extract @pbh/db, @pbh/payments, @pbh/linus from apps/funnel
[ ] Promote shared UI primitives to @pbh/ui
[ ] Build modal StepFlow state machine + 5 screens on marketing (open, transitions, terms-scroll gating, validation)
[ ] Tina landing block for 360-2502 (booking entry + Includes + $149)
[ ] Re-home 4 server actions to marketing; wire Stripe Embedded Checkout + webhook + Linus enrollment end-to-end
[ ] Reconcile design tokens
[ ] QA: test-mode payment through the modal (account -> consent row -> Stripe test card -> enrollment) + webhook backstop

RELATES TO: [deleted:pbh-bws.17] (signup/consent/payment surfaces — was 'no Figma', now superseded by these designs on marketing), [deleted:pbh-bws.20] (landing page), [deleted:pbh-bws.21] (account creation + consent), [deleted:pbh-bws.15] (component-library extension from V1), pbh-bws.24 (signed-token handoff), [deleted:pbh-bws.39] (Stripe Appearance/brand tokens)."}

{"id":"pbh-d5a","title":"Set up Playwright E2E to test the full onboarding flow (marketing -> funnel)","description":"Stand up Playwright end-to-end testing covering the whole onboarding flow across both apps: marketing booking (:3000) through the funnel handoff (:3001).

## Current state
- No E2E Playwright setup. "playwright" is present only transitively via @vitest/browser-playwright (Storybook vitest browser mode in apps/marketing) — there is NO @playwright/test, no playwright.config, no e2e specs, no root "test" script, and no CI (.github does not exist yet).
- Monorepo: pnpm@10.27 + Turborepo. Apps: marketing (:3000, tinacms dev), funnel (:3001).

## Setup
1. Add @playwright/test as a dev dependency and run npx playwright install (chromium at minimum).
2. Create an e2e location (e.g. top-level e2e/ or tests/e2e/) with playwright.config.ts. Use two webServer entries to boot marketing (:3000) and funnel (:3001) — or run against a shared "pnpm dev" — with baseURL per app / project.
3. Add a root "test:e2e" script and a Turborepo task (mark it non-cached / no outputs).
4. Add stable selectors (data-testid) to the booking form fields + step CTAs and the funnel pages as needed for reliable targeting.

## Happy-path spec (the "whole flow")
Marketing: land on the booking section -> fill signup (firstName, lastName, email) -> modal opens -> details step (DOB, ZIP, state, phone, gender, education, patient id) -> consent step (agree) -> payment step (Stripe Embedded Checkout, test card 4242 4242 4242 4242) -> done step -> click continue -> funnel /login?email= -> /assessments renders "Welcome Back, {firstName}".

Component/flow references: apps/marketing/src/components/booking/ (BookingStepFlow, Modal, DoneStep), packages/booking/src/ (SignupForm, DetailsForm, ConsentForm, PaymentStep), funnel apps/funnel/src/app/login + /assessments.

## Environment / infrastructure decisions & known hurdles (call out in implementation)
- Test DB: run against a DEDICATED test DB / Neon branch, NOT prod. Note: Vercel previews currently share the prod Neon DB, so do not point E2E at a preview URL that writes prod. Need per-run seeding + cleanup (users/consents/payments rows).
- Stripe: use TEST keys and an ACTIVE sandbox price (an archived/inactive price makes "start payment" fail — this bit us before). Decide how fulfillment is confirmed in tests: the onComplete verify path vs the webhook (STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET + stripe listen/forwarding). Interacting with the Stripe Checkout iframe for card entry needs frameLocator handling.
- Linus: the Linus sandbox API is US-only — enrollment 403s (surfacing as a webhook/enroll failure) unless the runner is on a US IP/VPN. For CI this likely requires stubbing/mocking Linus or a US-region runner; otherwise the enroll step of the full flow will fail.
- Secrets: Stripe test keys, DATABASE_URL (test branch), LINUS_* sandbox, NEXT_PUBLIC_FUNNEL_URL must be provided to the test env.

## CI (optional / follow-up)
No CI exists. Consider adding a GitHub Actions workflow to run the E2E suite on PRs (with the secrets above and playwright browsers cached). Can be split into its own task.

## Follow-up coverage
Once built, extend the suite to cover the new first-login welcome screen (pbh-chu) and the resume-at-first-incomplete-step booking behavior (pbh-bq8).

## Acceptance criteria
- @playwright/test installed; playwright.config.ts boots/targets both apps; "pnpm test:e2e" (or turbo run test:e2e) executes the suite locally.
- A green happy-path E2E drives marketing booking -> Stripe test payment -> funnel handoff -> /assessments.
- Test data is isolated (test DB/branch) and cleaned up between runs; docs/README note the required env + how to run.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"brizolla.tuily@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-07-20T18:16:34Z","created_by":"tuily","updated_at":"2026-07-20T19:28:19Z","external_ref":"https://linear.app/visualboston/issue/PBH-113"}

First, silent security degradation. hashIp (packages/booking/src/server/request-meta.ts:40-47) treats IP_HASH_SECRET as OPTIONAL and silently falls back to an unkeyed SHA-256. Over the ~4-billion IPv4 space that is a rainbow table, so the "hashed" IPs in audit_log.ip_hash and consents.ip_hash are effectively reversible to raw IPs. Nothing asserts the secret is present in production. AUTH_HANDOFF_SECRET has the same shape of problem: createAssessmentHandoffUrl catches its absence and falls back to the magic link (payment/actions.ts:103-108), so a misconfigured production degrades silently rather than failing.

{"id":"pbh-9yb.2","title":"Server-side identity for booking and assessment mutations","description":"resolveBookingUserId() (packages/booking/src/server/auth.ts:16-18) returns formData.get("userId") verbatim -- a client-controlled value, with a TODO(clerk) acknowledging it. Every exported server action downstream inherits it:

- detailsAction / consentAction (apps/marketing/src/components/booking/actions.ts:34-52) write PII and a consent record to an arbitrary account
- resendConfirmationAction mails an arbitrary address
- completeAssessmentSetup (apps/app/src/app/assessments/actions.ts:19-25) enrolls without ever calling auth()
- worst: createAssessmentHandoffUrl(userId) (apps/marketing/src/components/booking/payment/actions.ts:89-109) MINTS A SINGLE-USE LOGIN CREDENTIAL for any userId that has a succeeded, unconsumed payment (handoff.ts:115-134)

The only thing between an attacker and another customer's session is that user ids are random v4 UUIDs -- an unguessability defence, not an authorization control, and one that fails the moment a userId leaks through a log, a referrer, or a support ticket.

Marketing has no session, so the fix is not "call auth()": mint an HttpOnly, __Secure--prefixed, signed booking cookie server-side inside createAccountCore and have resolveBookingUserId read that instead.

SHIP THE 2-HOUR MITIGATION ON DAY 1 REGARDLESS of when the full cookie work lands: bind handoff issuance to the just-verified checkout session id plus a <=10-minute window since payment. That retires the session-takeover half on its own. Everything else here is a PII-integrity and spam problem, not a session-takeover one.

Closes checklist rows: Authorization enforced on every endpoint (incl. PHI report pull); Principle of least privilege; CSRF protections implemented; Secure session management.

* detailsAction / consentAction (apps/marketing/src/components/booking/actions.ts:34-52) write PII and a consent record to an arbitrary account
* resendConfirmationAction mails an arbitrary address
* completeAssessmentSetup (apps/app/src/app/assessments/actions.ts:19-25) enrolls without ever calling auth()
* worst: createAssessmentHandoffUrl(userId) (apps/marketing/src/components/booking/payment/actions.ts:89-109) MINTS A SINGLE-USE LOGIN CREDENTIAL for any userId that has a succeeded, unconsumed payment (handoff.ts:115-134)

The only thing between an attacker and another customer's session is that user ids are random v4 UUIDs -- an unguessability defence, not an authorization control, and one that fails the moment a userId leaks through a log, a referrer, or a support ticket.

Marketing has no session, so the fix is not "call auth()": mint an HttpOnly, __Secure--prefixed, signed booking cookie server-side inside createAccountCore and have resolveBookingUserId read that instead.

SHIP THE 2-HOUR MITIGATION ON DAY 1 REGARDLESS of when the full cookie work lands: bind handoff issuance to the just-verified checkout session id plus a <=10-minute window since payment. That retires the session-takeover half on its own. Everything else here is a PII-integrity and spam problem, not a session-takeover one.

Closes checklist rows: Authorization enforced on every endpoint (incl. PHI report pull); Principle of least privilege; CSRF protections implemented; Secure session management.

## Acceptance Criteria

createAccountCore sets a signed HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=lax booking cookie carrying the userId, TTL <= 2h. resolveBookingUserId no longer reads formData -- it reads and verifies the cookie, with no fallback to the form value. Hidden userId inputs removed from the details, consent, and payment step forms. createAssessmentHandoffUrl takes NO userId argument and additionally requires the checkout session id verified in the same request, so a handoff can only be minted for a payment this browser just completed. completeAssessmentSetup calls await auth() and ignores any form-supplied userId. resendConfirmationAction derives its recipient from the cookie. {"id":"pbh-7l6","title":"Test the track-selection helpers in @pbh/copy","description":"packages/copy/src/track.ts has zero tests. Only two test files exist in the repo (packages/copy/src/lexicon.test.ts, packages/booking/src/packages.test.ts) and neither touches parseTrack, isTrack, higherTrack, highestTrack, or TRACK_RANK.

WHY THIS MATTERS
The banned-terms guard verifies the words are right. Nothing verifies the track selection that feeds them. A wrong TRACK_RANK, or a highestTrack([]) that returned a track instead of null, would render the wrong product's vocabulary to a paying user - the exact failure @pbh/copy exists to prevent - and every existing test would stay green.

These are entitlement decisions, not formatting:
- packages/booking/src/server/entitlement.ts:40 calls highestTrack over a user's succeeded payment rows
- packages/booking/src/server/register-and-enroll.ts:459 calls parseTrack on a DB column

Each helper's doc comment already states behaviour nothing asserts.

ADD packages/copy/src/track.test.ts COVERING
- parseTrack returns null for unknown strings, null, undefined, numbers, objects - never a default track. The comment is explicit that silently falling back to one of the two products is the failure this mapping exists to prevent.
- isTrack narrows correctly for both valid values and rejects everything else.
- higherTrack is correct in both argument orders and when both args are equal.
- highestTrack([]) returns null (no succeeded payment = no entitlement, callers must render pre-purchase copy). Also: single-element, all-wellness, mixed, and order-independence for a mixed list.
- TRACK_RANK orders wellness below clinical, and TRACKS is ordered lowest to highest entitlement - these two must agree with each other.

Consider also pinning that copyFor throws (rather than silently rendering) when handed a term key from outside the type system, e.g. a value read from a DB column or Tina field: resolve.ts:42-43 does TERMS[track][key] then entry.many, so an unknown key is a TypeError. Loud is the right behaviour; it is just undocumented.

Follows the PR-feedback work on tuily/track-copy-mapping (d811b59, e98fc7c).","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"brizolla.tuily@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-08-05T12:53:10Z","created_by":"tuily","updated_at":"2026-08-05T12:53:10Z"}
